items.title: A credit-balance 400 is not the usage-limit wall, and every run pays for that.
items.detail: 2026-08-23: all three crons died with `Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API` and exited 1, so the day went red and the episode only shipped from a manual dispatch at 14:42 UTC, six hours late. `_usage_limit_reset` keys on the string `usage limit`, which this message does not contain, so `check_api_budget()` printed "preflight inconclusive — continuing" and the run went on to spend 40 article body fetches, ~37 Brave enrichment calls and an agentic research call before failing at the script call — three times over, which is the exact waste the preflight was written to prevent (see its docstring on 2026-07-25). Match the credit-balance refusal too and exit `EXIT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`; the workflow already turns 75 into a skipped day with a warning instead of a failure.

items.title: The review goes quiet on exactly the days worth reviewing.
items.detail: `main()` only fetches a job log from a run whose conclusion is `success`. On 2026-08-23 there was no such run, so the review published a bare trigger table and no narrative — three failures and not a word about why. Fall back to the newest failed run's log (the facts are all there: the 400 above is in it), and keep the successful-run preference for ordinary days.

items.title: The review cannot see the run that made the episode when a cron did not.
items.detail: It is gated on the third cron, so 2026-08-23's manual dispatch four hours later is absent from the write-up and from the archive. Either widen `fetch_runs` past `event: schedule` for the day, or make the review re-runnable for a date and re-publish over the same file (`--date` already exists; the index and feed update in place).

items.title: The review reports itself as an unfinished run.
items.detail: The `review` job runs inside the 3:05 AM cron's own workflow run, so every review to date ends with "Fallback 2 … in_progress" and the narrative reads it as a pending unknown ("a third in progress at review time", 2026-08-20). `summarize_runs` knows `GITHUB_RUN_ID`; label that row as the reviewing run so the model stops treating it as a cliffhanger.

items.title: Decide what to do about scheduler drift.
items.detail: Every trigger in the sample started late: +44/+29/+32 (08-20), +46/+31/+31 (08-21), +34/+20/+25 (08-22), +35/+22/+25 (08-23). This is GitHub's scheduled-run queue, not the pipeline, and the reviews report it as a fault every single day. Either move the crons earlier and accept the drift as the schedule, or keep the number and stop framing it as one — a fact reported daily as a problem and never acted on trains the reader to skip the paragraph.

items.title: Watch the four 2026-08-22 fixes on air.
items.detail: None has been observed in a shipped episode: the runs the day after all died at the credit wall. The first green day's review is the check — citation alignment should land near 51%/55% rather than 5-8/15 and 0-1/deep dive, `tts_short_segments` should be ~2% of segments rather than 13 of 16, and the canary should only pin OpenAI after two timeouts per model.

items.title: Gemini has not rendered an episode in the review window.
items.detail: 08-20, 08-21 and 08-22 all pinned OpenAI on canary read timeouts against `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`; 08-23 never got that far. The probe item under Short-term is the diagnostic — the reviews now give it a daily before/after record, so run it and read the next week's reviews rather than re-reasoning about the ladder.

items.title: All three scheduled triggers failed or did not complete on August 26th.
items.detail: The primary run (08:54 UTC) and Fallback 1 (09:40 UTC) both concluded in failure. Fallback 2 (10:40 UTC) was still in progress at the last update (10:44 UTC), meaning no episode was produced for the day. Three consecutive attempts to execute the pipeline all either failed or remained unfinished, which suggests a systematic problem rather than transient flakiness. Check the run logs at https://github.com/zirnhelt/curated-podcast-generator/actions/runs/32950154292 and https://github.com/zirnhelt/curated-podcast-generator/actions/runs/32954282339 to identify the failure mode that struck both the primary and first fallback identically.

items.title: Gemini TTS rate limit (HTTP 429) triggered twice on canary checks, forcing full OpenAI render.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, the Gemini TTS pre-flight check failed with HTTP 429 errors on two separate canary attempts. The pipeline's fallback logic caught both failures before audio synthesis began and switched the entire episode to OpenAI rather than risk a mid-episode voice change. The mechanism is clear: Gemini's quota was exhausted before the render stage. To close this, either increase the Gemini quota tier for the API key, implement request queuing to respect rate limits, or add a secondary Gemini endpoint (via Vertex AI) as a separate capacity pool.

items.title: Roundup story order drifted again despite a repair pass, with 3 of 15 stories airing out of sequence.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, the script/roundup-order segment failed once, was repaired, and still shipped with 3 stories in the wrong position relative to their assigned blocks. Of 15 roundup citations total, 13 matched their sources, but the 3 misaligned stories suggest the repair pass did not fully resolve the ordering logic. The deep dive citations fared worse: 0 of 3 matched. The root cause is in the roundup ordering algorithm—either it does not persist constraints across repair cycles, or the repair itself reintroduces drift. Trace the sort order during and after the repair pass to identify whether the issue is in the initial sort, the repair logic, or both.

items.title: Brave Answers API hit its usage limit partway through the run, forcing a fallback to web snippets.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, the script/brave-answers segment failed with HTTP 402 (usage limit exceeded) after the quota was exhausted. The pipeline switched to web snippets for all remaining answers in that episode. The 402 error itself indicates the account hit its hard limit, not a transient failure. Confirm the quota tier on the Brave account, assess whether the episode's answer count is typical, and decide whether to increase the quota, implement batching, or rely on web snippets as the primary source when the API is unavailable.

items.title: One TTS segment returned audio shorter than its word count predicts, requiring a retry.
items.detail: On 2026-08-27, one text-to-speech take produced audio duration shorter than the word count would estimate. The pipeline retried once per protocol and the issue resolved. This is a single occurrence and may be transient voice synthesis variance. If this recurs across multiple segments or runs, it signals either a systematic issue in duration estimation, a problem with a particular voice model, or the TTS API's handling of edge-case text. Monitor for recurrence; if it persists, audit the duration formula against actual TTS output and consider adding a tolerance band before flagging a retry.
